text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if you have noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, or changes in the color of your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your history of ulcerative colitis, have you noticed any darkening of your urine or light-colored stools, which can indicate bile duct issues?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have confirmed signs of jaundice and severe itching. Given your history of ulcerative colitis, have you experienced any recent abdominal pain or changes in bowel habits?

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of alcohol use or current medication use, including supplements? Also, have you noticed any fever or right upper quadrant pain?

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of severe pruritus, jaundice, and a history of ulcerative colitis strongly points toward a cholestatic liver disease. To confirm the specific type of cholestasis, I need to see the pattern of your liver enzymes. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: The markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase with mild transaminase elevation confirms a cholestatic pattern, which, combined with your history of ulcerative colitis, strongly suggests Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. I will order specific serological tests to rule out autoimmune hepatitis and confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Antimitochondrial_Antibody, Anti-Smooth_Muscle_Antibody, p-ANCA

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative antimitochondrial antibodies help rule out Primary Biliary Cholangitis, while the negative ANA and your strong association with ulcerative colitis make Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis the most likely diagnosis. I will request imaging to visualize the bile ducts for confirmation. REQUEST IMAGES
